audience_note: Built for the project owner's own machine. The installed Plithos corpus carries material whose redistribution rights have not been reviewed, so this bundle is not cleared for publication or for handing to a third party.
runtime_self_contained_note: Nothing in this bundle requires LM Studio, Git, a system Python, a GitHub account, or any download once it is installed. Everything it needs is inside the folder.

network.note: The Web fallback exists in the application and ships switched off with no credential. An installed Uvaha reaches nothing outside the machine unless the owner turns it on himself. The model endpoint is loopback only and the application refuses any other host.

python.why: The application is Python. An embedded interpreter is what removes the system Python from the requirements.

llama_cpp.why: The CPU build answers, and on this hardware it answers in minutes. The same official release publishes a Vulkan build, and a 4.47 GB Q4_K_M fits a Radeon 890M whole. The CPU manifest stays beside this one as the rollback, because a bundle that starts slowly beats one that does not start.
llama_cpp.sha256_provenance: Reported by the other agent working this repository, not verified here. The build verifies it on download: if it is wrong the build stops and says the published bytes have changed, which is the answer either way.
llama_cpp.server_flags_note: --n-gpu-layers all asks for the whole model on the GPU. Swapping in a Vulkan-capable binary and hoping it chooses that placement is not the same request. Whether it was granted is visible in llama-server's own startup output, which this bundle prints to the window it runs in: a Vulkan device and a layer count. Zero offloaded layers means the experiment failed, whatever the response time.

model.conversion_route: llama.cpp via the GGUF-my-repo space on Hugging Face
model.why: Q4_K_M rather than the Q8_0 the model manifest pins, because it fits a consumer GPU whole and the Q8 does not. The Q8 measurement stays in config/model_olmo2_7b_instruct.v1.json as the CPU baseline this is compared against.
model.verification_note: AllenAI publishes safetensors, not GGUF, so every GGUF of this model is a third-party conversion. The conversion route is recorded because that, not the uploader's name, is what can be checked.

corpus.why: The evidence. Pinned by the same commit the application asserts, so a bundle cannot quietly carry a different corpus from the one it claims.

verification.note: UNVERIFIED is not a value the builder accepts. It is written here so the shape of the manifest is reviewable before the artifacts are in hand, and so a half-filled manifest fails loudly rather than producing a bundle nobody can check.

acceptance.note: A Vulkan asset in the manifest is not evidence of GPU inference. The measurement is llama-server naming a Vulkan device and a non-zero offloaded layer count, and the same question answered faster than the CPU build's measured time on the same machine.
